fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Robert Taylor's Precession Arithmetic", "body": "Episode twenty two closes the hosts' fourteen part walk through Reverend Robert Taylor's Astronomical Theological Lectures, written by a preacher who went to jail for arguing that scripture encodes the sky. Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio read Taylor's arithmetic on the precession of the equinoxes, roughly seventy one years and eight months for a degree and two thousand one hundred sixty years for a whole sign, which he uses to push Saint Anne's day, the twenty sixth of July, back some thirteen thousand years. Both hosts lean away from that antiquity, suspecting later scholars back calculated the figures the way a blogger backdates a post."}, {"title": "Midnight Stable of Capricorn", "body": "Taylor fixes the nativity at the minute of midnight when the sun, having passed its lowest declination, enters the first degree of Capricorn the goat, the same moment Egyptians gave Osiris, Persians gave Mithra and Greeks gave Bacchus. Dylan Saccoccio adds an observer's correction: Capricorn sits below the horizon at that hour, so what actually stands overhead is Cancer, whose asterisms and star names carry a stable, a manger and donkeys. Virgo rises on the eastern border at midnight and reaches the midheaven by dawn, which the hosts read as birth from the mother's side, echoed in Justin Martyr's cave near Bethlehem."}, {"title": "The Fish Goat of Nazareth", "body": "Dylan Saccoccio argues that Nazareth reads as a mystical term rather than a town, noting it never appears in the Old Testament, the Talmud or the writings of Josephus, and that lexicons concede its etymology is unknown. Reading the odd Greek terminations through a Latin and Celtic lens, he splits the word into nun, the Hebrew letter meaning fish and progeny, az meaning goat, and rot meaning wheel, giving a fish goat on the wheel that answers Capricorn the sea goat. Chance Garton counters with a simpler letter swap, from N to M, landing on Mazzaroth, the Hebrew word for the zodiac."}, {"title": "Marine Venus Becomes Virgin Mary", "body": "Taylor traces Mary's line through Anna the prophetess, daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, which the hosts render as the year, daughter of our shining god, in the constellation of Virgo. The argument then runs through Miriam and waters, Maria and seas, and Virgo Marina, virgin of the sea, out to the lost painting of the marine Venus by Apelles, modeled on Campaspe and later placed in a temple by Augustus. Taylor sets the pagan hymn of Lucretius beside the litany that still hails Mary as queen of heaven, star of the sea and morning star."}, {"title": "Erasmus and the Twelve Gates", "body": "Before reaching New Jerusalem, the hosts cite Bishop Herbert Marsh on Erasmus, whose five New Testament editions between 1516 and 1535 reworked Revelation so heavily that ninety of a hundred alterations in the 1527 printing fell in that single book. On that footing Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio read Revelation twenty one as a sky map: twelve gates carrying the names of the twelve tribes, twelve wall foundations carrying the apostles, and the sixth gate, the harvest month, yielded to the miraculously fruitful virgin, Virgo. The gate stones and their birthstone matches wait for the members half."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The manger, the twelve gates, and the Virgin Mary all trace back to the same sky. Closing their fourteen-part walk through Reverend Robert Taylor's astronomical lectures, Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio read the nativity as a midnight star chart, Nazareth as a zodiac cipher, and Revelation's New Jerusalem as twelve gates keyed to the twelve tribes and the twelve signs.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this episode: the procession of the equinoxes and how Taylor used it to date scripture, the meaning of Nazareth and the analemma, the symbolism of the resurrection across ancient traditions, the Virgin of the Sea and her connection to Mary, the queen of heaven and the language shared between pagan and Christian liturgies, the documented history of how the Book of Revelation came together, and the 12 gates of New Jerusalem mapped onto the zodiac and the birthstones of each sign. The closing segment also looks at the natal chart of Inner Whirled itself and what the moment of its launch may reveal about the show’s purpose.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Twelve Gates and the Birthstones of Revelation", "body": "Revelation 21 describes a city with twelve gates, twelve angels, twelve tribal names and three gates on each of the four sides, which reads as the four quarters of the zodiac rather than as architecture. The twelve foundation stones are walked in order, jasper as bloodstone for Aries, sapphire for Taurus, chalcedony for Gemini, on through amethyst for Pisces, and the list matches the modern birthstone table almost exactly, with chrysoprase for Capricorn and jacinth for Aquarius among the few later substitutions. It gets called the least disputable astro-theological passage in the whole Bible."}, {"title": "The Middleman System and the Price of Trust", "body": "The admission that nobody can check the Greek originals, because the manuscripts they were supposedly copied from no longer exist, opens onto a far larger pattern. Every industry is built the same way, with medicine, technology and scholarship all arranged so that you must trust a credentialed expert rather than do the work yourself, and the incentive to lie in order to hold a competitive advantage is never acknowledged. Dylan names this the Baal system, a fractal of middlemen standing between a person and the source of anything, and both hosts treat the erosion of ordinary trust as the real damage."}, {"title": "Apollo of the Streets and the Gatekeeper Gods", "body": "The streets of gold become the ecliptic once Apollo carries the epithet Ageus, he of the streets, and the same god surfaces as Abulu, a Babylonian word for gate, guarding doorways as a conical obelisk hung with ribbons that looks exactly like the Beltane maypole they had just examined. Terminus, Janus and Saturn turn out to be the same boundary keeper under other names, and the conclusion drawn is that there are not many gods but one system, the sun as a single actor playing every character the calendar calls for."}, {"title": "No One Is Speaking in Exodus 20", "body": "Read in Hebrew, the opening of the commandments gives YHWH, then a word whose feminine ending would render as goddess, then Asher, which translators quietly convert into the pronoun who. There is no I am anywhere in the line and no narrator either, so the familiar English sentence is an invention laid over three divine names. Alongside it sits Augustine conceding in City of God that the learned pagans already held every god and goddess to be parts of one Jupiter, which makes Christianity a consolidation of what came before rather than a break from it."}, {"title": "Amun the Hidden Inside the Word Amen", "body": "Taylor traces Amun through Ammon, Amen, Mon and Man, splitting it into Am the fire and On the sun, which puts a sun god inside the word every congregation says at the close of a prayer. Manetho and Plutarch both report that the name signifies concealed, which suits a sun crucified at the autumn equinox, hidden through winter and reborn in the manger of the goat on the twenty fifth of December. The challenge offered is chronological, since the Hebrew spelling does not enter the record before the tenth century while the Greek accounts are a thousand years older."}]
